description: Jonathan Busch published HeatSupply to model the development of district-heating networks in cities. The catalogue summary identifies local authorities, commercial developers and community organisations as the three types of actors that initiate network development. The model page points to an Energy Policy paper and supporting material containing an ODD protocol. Coverage is an urban network-development setting; the inspected metadata does not establish a transferable calibration, a fixed geographic grid or an annual simulation period. It supports agent-based study of how different initiators affect heat-network development. The release lists NetLogo as its platform, while its legacy language field says other; the record retains that distinction. Release 1.1.0 is available free through the CoMSES code repository and lists NetLogo. The release licence is CC-BY-4.0. Source code and model data were not downloaded or executed. Related resources include the CoMSES computational model library.
